notes:
Source: Telos Alliance / Linear Acoustic "AERO Family Owner's Guide" v3.32.25 (official manual, AERO.2000 rear-panel connector list p.21 + connector pinout tables p.95-97 + specifications table p.92-94), cross-checked against the manufacturer product page https://www.telosalliance.com/Linear/AERO2000. AERO.2000 is a 2RU broadcast audio/loudness processing platform (AEROMAX loudness control, UPMAX upmixing, optional Dolby D/D+ encode/transcode, Nielsen/Verance watermarking) with single SDI I/O path (de-embed/re-embed up to 16 audio channels) plus 8 main AES3 channels on BNC and 8 auxiliary AES3 channels (9-16) on a DB25 breakout.

Two rear-panel connectors were omitted from the port list because the manual explicitly documents them as non-functional: a DB9 "Analog I/O" (stereo +4dBu, "currently not used") and a spare "Reserved" RJ45 ("reserved for future use, not connected internally").

Two ports (AES I/O DB25 aux and GPI/O DB25) have no true match in the allowed connector-id list, since it contains no generic D-sub id — "aes3" and "rs232" were used as the closest available approximations respectively; see each port's note for the real physical connector (25-pin female D-sub in both cases).

PSU inlet connector style (assumed IEC C14) is inferred, not manufacturer-confirmed in the reviewed text. USB front-panel connector type is likewise a reasonable assumption (USB-A), not explicitly specified.

ports.name: Metadata I/O
ports.note: RS-485 Dolby serial metadata (SMPTE RDD6), pinout per SMPTE 207M, 115.2 kbps, physical connector is DB9-F

ports.name: SDI In
ports.note: auto-sensing SD or HD (SMPTE 292M/259M); AERO.2000 does not support 3G-SDI (that's on AERO.20/200/2400)

ports.name: AES3 Ref
ports.note: 48 kHz DARS or any AES3 reference signal

ports.name: ENC Out
ports.note: encoder output, fed in parallel with AES 15/16

ports.name: Vref
ports.note: video reference input; documented in manual as "not currently supported"

ports.name: LTC In
ports.note: LTC timecode input; documented in manual as "not currently supported"

ports.name: AES I/O
ports.note: auxiliary AES3 channels 9-16 (4 pairs, in+out on same connector), unbalanced, per SMPTE 276M/AES-3ID-2001. Physical connector is a 25-pin female D-sub (DB25); no D-sub id exists in the allowed connector list, so "aes3" was chosen as the closest functional match.

ports.name: GPI/O
ports.note: 8 GPI inputs + 8 GPO outputs, 0-5V TTL, pull-to-ground activation. Physical connector is a 25-pin female D-sub (DB25) carrying parallel TTL contact-closure I/O, not RS-232 serial data; no D-sub/GPIO id exists in the allowed connector list, so "rs232" was chosen only as the closest D-sub-shaped control connector.

ports.name: Headphone Out
ports.note: front panel, +12 dBu max, with volume control

ports.name: USB
ports.note: front panel; exact USB type/purpose not detailed in the manual excerpt reviewed, USB-A assumed

ports.name: PSU1
ports.note: one of two redundant AC inlets, 100-240 VAC 50/60 Hz auto-sensing, 175W max combined. Exact IEC inlet style (e.g. C13/C14) not explicitly stated in the manual; assumed standard IEC C14, typical of dual-redundant broadcast PSU modules.

ports.name: PSU2
ports.note: second of two redundant AC inlets, see PSU1
